subject.title: improve(gateway): tunable control-plane write rate limit, default unchanged

question: Should OpenClaw expose a gateway-global control-plane write quota up to 600 per minute, or require batching or a more narrowly scoped trusted-automation mechanism?
rationale: Tests establish the implementation mechanics, but they cannot choose how much authenticated control-plane abuse protection operators may disable or whether a gateway-global setting is the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Approve bounded global quota
options.body: Accept the unchanged default, bounded range, per-identity enforcement, hot adoption, and explicit warning that every identity receives the configured limit.

options.title: Design scoped automation policy
options.body: Replace the global setting with an identity-, capability-, or credential-scoped higher quota for specifically trusted automation.

options.title: Retain fixed safety limit
options.body: Decline the new configuration surface and keep batching as the supported path for atomic configuration changes.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded global quota
recommendation.body: Accept the unchanged default, bounded range, per-identity enforcement, hot adoption, and explicit warning that every identity receives the configured limit.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the strongest available routing candidate from the gateway security and configuration history for choosing the permanent trust boundary.
